note: Watchdog Prune deletes rows from the core watchdog (dblog) table on cron (watchdog_prune_cron). Config object watchdog_prune.settings has two keys: watchdog_prune_age (global 'older than' relative-date string, default -18 MONTHS) and watchdog_prune_age_type (newline-separated type|age rules, e.g. 'php|-1 MONTH'). Configure route watchdog_prune.watchdog_prune_settings at /admin/config/development/watchdog-prune, permission 'administer watchdog prune'. No config schema and no default config ship, so the config object is created on first save. Requires core dblog 'Database log messages to keep' (dblog.settings:row_limit) = All (0). No Drush command. Medium/hard cases write/read watchdog_prune.settings; baseline is that the config object does not exist, so cleanup/reset delete it.

evals.prompt: How and when does the Drupal watchdog_prune module delete log entries, and which config keys control it?
evals.expected_output: It deletes rows from the watchdog (dblog) table on each cron run (hook watchdog_prune_cron). It is controlled by watchdog_prune.settings: watchdog_prune_age (global 'delete entries older than' age, default -18 MONTHS) and watchdog_prune_age_type (per-type type|age rules). There is no Drush command.

evals.prompt: I enabled watchdog_prune but old log entries are still being removed by row count, not by age. What Drupal core logging setting must be changed for watchdog_prune to work as intended?
evals.expected_output: Core dblog's 'Database log messages to keep' (dblog.settings:row_limit, at admin/config/development/logging) must be set to All (0). Otherwise core trims the watchdog table by row count and undermines watchdog_prune's age-based pruning.

evals.prompt: In watchdog_prune, how do I tell it to prune only 'php' log entries older than one month while keeping other types longer? What is the exact format for the per-type setting?
evals.expected_output: Use the 'Delete watchdog entries by type' setting (watchdog_prune_age_type), one rule per line in the form type|age, e.g. php|-1 MONTH. Per-type rules run first and are excluded from the global age rule, so php is pruned at 1 month while other types follow watchdog_prune_age.

evals.prompt: This site has watchdog_prune configured. Inspect the live configuration and state the global age threshold after which watchdog entries are deleted.
evals.expected_output: watchdog_prune.settings:watchdog_prune_age is '-6 MONTHS', i.e. entries older than 6 months are pruned on cron.

evals.prompt: On this site watchdog_prune has one or more per-type prune rules configured. Inspect the live configuration and state which watchdog log type has a per-type rule and what age it uses.
evals.expected_output: watchdog_prune.settings:watchdog_prune_age_type contains 'php|-1 MONTH', so the php log type is pruned after 1 month.

evals.prompt: Configure watchdog_prune on this site so that, on cron, it deletes watchdog log entries older than 3 months. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Set watchdog_prune.settings:watchdog_prune_age to '-3 MONTHS' (via the settings form at /admin/config/development/watchdog-prune or by saving the config), then save.
evals.difficulty_note: verify passes when watchdog_prune_age is a 3-month age (matches /3\s*month/i).

evals.prompt: On my site I want the 'php' log messages to be cleared out once they are older than a month, using the Watchdog Prune module. Set that up on the live site.
evals.expected_output: Add a per-type rule 'php|-1 MONTH' to watchdog_prune.settings:watchdog_prune_age_type (the 'Delete watchdog entries by type' field), then save.
evals.difficulty_note: verify passes when watchdog_prune_age_type contains a php rule with a 1-month age (matches /php\s*\|/i and /1\s*month/i).
